name: Microsoft 365 Defender: pull alerts
description: Every 5 minutes, reads new Microsoft Defender XDR alerts (Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, Identity, Cloud Apps, Entra ID Protection, Sentinel when onboarded) from Microsoft Graph `security/alerts_v2` and creates one pending alert per Defender alert.

params.label: Entra tenant ID
params.help: Directory (tenant) ID from Entra admin center > Overview.

secrets.name: MS_CLIENT_ID
secrets.description: Application (client) ID of the Entra app registration used to read alerts.

secrets.name: MS_CLIENT_SECRET
secrets.description: Client secret value of that app registration used to read alerts.

setup:
### Entra side
1. Entra admin center > App registrations > **New registration** (single tenant, no redirect URI).
2. API permissions > Add a permission > Microsoft Graph > **Application permissions**: `SecurityAlert.Read.All`.
3. Click **Grant admin consent for <tenant>** (application permissions do nothing until an admin consents).
4. Certificates & secrets > **New client secret**; copy the secret *value* (not its ID). Note its expiry date.

### Here
1. Settings > Secrets: add the client ID and client secret below. Each must allow **both** `login.microsoftonline.com` (token request) and `graph.microsoft.com` (API call): the OAuth token is bound to the same hosts as the secrets that obtained it.
2. Install with `AZURE_TENANT_ID` = the Directory (tenant) ID.

Token: `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token` with `grant_type=client_credentials`, `scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/.default` ([client credentials flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-client-creds-grant-flow)). The token is cached per worker until shortly before it expires and never stored.

### What it calls
`GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2?$filter=createdDateTime ge <previous run>&$top=100`. Each alert becomes an alert with source `m365-defender`, external id = the Graph alert `id`, title = `title (serviceSource)`, severity: high → high, medium → medium, low → low, informational → info, unknown → medium. The full Graph alert (including `evidence`) is the payload, so the identity triage template can find the user principal in `userAccount` evidence.

### Limits
ponytail: one page per run (`$top=100`); `@odata.nextLink` is not followed, so more than 100 new alerts in 5 minutes are cut off. The window is on `createdDateTime`, so an alert that Graph exposes later than its creation time can fall between two runs. Graph allows 150 requests per minute per app per tenant on security alerts. A non-200 answer (bad credentials, missing consent, 429) creates nothing and fails the run with the HTTP status; the next run re-reads the window from the last successful run (at most 24 h back).

Docs: [List alerts_v2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-list-alerts_v2?view=graph-rest-1.0), [alert resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/security-alert?view=graph-rest-1.0), [Throttling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits#security-detections-and-incidents-service-limits).
